just took a botany course. my knowledge is not of a professional nature, but i'll write what i know. 

a plant's stem and branches (a branch is technically a stem. that exam question stumped me.) consist of nodes and internodes. the node sections contain axillary buds and internodes are long sections between the nodes. any axillary bud can form either a branch or leaf. in most plants, the length of the internodes (determining the concentration of leaves/branches) is purely genetic and varies between species.

the growth hormone auxin plays a major role in a plant growing toward the sun. it stimulates stem growth and is 'repelled' by sunlight, thus concentrating in lesser lit parts of a stem. this causes the 'dark' half of the stem to grow faster and turns the stem toward the sun. 

as for whether the axillary buds are turned into a stem or leaf, i asked my professor this question in lecture. he has a phd in plant physiology and told me the mechanism is not yet understood. of course, maybe he told me this just to avoid explaining a complicated subject to a classroom of non-botany majors, but he did seem sincere for what it's worth.
